QBR — Kellerman Industrial (CLI-0042), Q1 2025. Account owner: Marcus Trent.
Tense call. The Jan 14-16 Chicago storm delayed a large batch of Kellerman freight (a representative affected shipment is linked on this note) and the client raised the jackknife incident (INC-2025-00417) directly. On-time for January will breach the 97.0% target. Client asked, pointedly, whether Meridian can handle their peak volumes. Committed to an SLA credit per contract CON-0042-01 and a written recovery plan. Sentiment concerned; first real crack in the relationship this year.

QBR — Kellerman Industrial (CLI-0042), Q1 2025. Account owner: Marcus Trent.
Q1 review with Kellerman. January storm credit applied and closed out. On-time recovering but still below the 97% target. Client cautious but constructive. Watching. Contract CON-0042-01.

QBR — Kellerman Industrial (CLI-0042), Q2 2025. Account owner: Marcus Trent.
Q2 review. On-time slipped again despite no major weather. Kellerman flagged three late LTL loads this quarter and rising ticket volume. Moved account health to 'watch'. Asked for a concrete improvement plan by next QBR. Contract CON-0042-01.

QBR — Kellerman Industrial (CLI-0042), Q3 2025. Account owner: Marcus Trent.
Q3 review. Trend is clearly down — on-time now materially under target and the client is openly evaluating alternatives. Escalated to 'at-risk'. This is now a retention situation; a formal save plan is attached. Contract CON-0042-01.

ACCOUNT SAVE PLAN — Kellerman Industrial (CLI-0042), contract CON-0042-01.
Situation: strategic LTL account degraded from healthy to at-risk over 2025. Root causes: the January Chicago storm (INC-2025-00417), a summer run of late loads, and rising support-ticket volume without a systemic fix.
Plan: (1) dedicated CHI capacity for Kellerman freight during peak; (2) weekly on-time scorecard shared with the client; (3) executive sponsor check-in; (4) goodwill credit beyond contractual minimums. Owner: Marcus Trent. Review at Q4 QBR.
